changes.text: 魏安釐王二十年，魏公子无忌带着百余乘车骑出了大梁城，准备去秦军阵前拼命，与赵国同归于尽。车过城东的夷门，他停下来见守门的老人侯嬴，把这打算原原本本告诉了他。侯嬴只送了一句「公子勉之矣，老臣不能從」。车队走出几里，《史记》写无忌「心不快」；他掉转车头，回来问侯嬴。

In the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei, Prince Wuji rode out of the city of Daliang with a hundred-odd chariots and horsemen, intending to hurl himself at the Qin army and die alongside the state of Zhao. Passing the Yimen, the eastern gate of the city, he stopped to see Hou Ying, the aged gatekeeper there, and told him the plan outright. Hou Ying saw him off with a single line — "Push on, my lord; I am old and cannot follow you". The column had gone a few li when the Records of the Grand Historian has Wuji "troubled in his heart"; he turned the chariots around and came back to ask Hou Ying what he had missed.
难处摆在那里：秦军围住赵都邯郸，魏王已经派将军晋鄙率十万大军救赵，却传令止步，把军队留在邺观望。无忌手里没有兵，只有百余乘车骑和一群门客。去是送死；不去，邯郸旦暮可下，而他的姐姐是赵国平原君的夫人。

The difficulty was plain to see. Qin forces had invested Handan, the Zhao capital. King Anxi had already sent General Jin Pi with a hundred thousand troops to relieve Zhao, then ordered him to halt and camp at Ye and watch. Wuji had no army, only a hundred-odd chariots and a band of retainers. Riding out meant dying for nothing. Staying meant Handan could fall any day — and his own sister was Lord Pingyuan's wife.
秦昭王在破赵长平军之后，进兵围邯郸。无忌的姐姐是平原君夫人，她几次写信给魏王和无忌求救。魏王于是派将军晋鄙将十万众救赵。

King Zhao of Qin, having destroyed Zhao's army at Changping, marched on and laid siege to Handan. Wuji's sister was the wife of Lord Pingyuan. She wrote letter after letter to the King of Wei and to Wuji begging for help, and the king sent General Jin Pi with a hundred thousand troops to rescue Zhao.
平原君的使者一批接一批赶到魏国，冠盖相属，责备公子说：我高攀这门婚姻，是以为公子高义、能急人之困；如今邯郸旦暮降秦而魏国救兵不至，这份高义在哪里？哪怕你看不起我赵胜，独不怜公子姊邪——难道连你的姐姐也不可怜吗？

Lord Pingyuan's envoys now arrived in Wei in an unbroken stream, official carriages crowding the road, and reproached the prince in their master's name: I attached myself to this marriage because I took the prince for a man of high principle, one who hurries to relieve another's distress. Now Handan may surrender to Qin any day and Wei's rescue has not come — where is that principle? "Even if you think little of me, Zhao Sheng, have you no pity for your own sister?"

魏国有位隐士侯嬴，年七十，家贫，在大梁夷门守门。无忌想厚赠他，他不肯收，说自己修身絜行几十年，终不能因为守门穷困而受财。无忌于是置酒大会宾客，空出车上左边的尊位，亲自去迎侯嬴。侯嬴穿着破旧衣冠，径直登上上座，也不谦让，为的是看无忌的反应；无忌执辔，愈恭。侯嬴又在集市上故意站了很久，让过路人都来围观；无忌的脸色始终不变。到家后无忌请他坐上座，向在座宾客一一介绍，宾客皆惊。侯嬴后来自己说破：他这样做是想成全公子礼贤下士的名声；市人因此把他看作小人，称无忌是能下士的长者。宴罢，侯嬴成为上客。

Wei had a recluse named Hou Ying, seventy years old and poor, a gatekeeper at the Yimen. Wuji sought him out and tried to present him with a handsome gift. Hou Ying would not take it: he had kept himself and his conduct clean for decades, he said, and would not accept the prince's money simply because gatekeeping left him poor. So Wuji laid on a feast for all his retainers, and once the guests were seated, he went out with his carriage and escort, left the seat of honor on the left of the chariot empty, and fetched Hou Ying himself. Hou Ying, in his shabby robe and cap, climbed straight up into that seat without a word of demur — a test of Wuji, this was — and Wuji took the reins and grew only more respectful. Hou Ying then stood about a long time in the marketplace so that passers-by would stare; Wuji's manner never changed. At the house Wuji showed Hou Ying to the seat of honor and presented him to the assembled guests one by one, and the guests were astonished. Hou Ying later spelled out his reasoning: he was a mere gatekeeper, and the prince had personally come for him before a crowd. "I wanted to make your name," he said, "so I stood a long time by your carriage in the market while people watched, and the more I tried you, the more respectful you became. The townsfolk took me for a lout and you for a true elder who can humble himself before scholars." When the feast broke up, Hou Ying became one of Wuji's most honored guests.
折回夷门之后，侯嬴献上一个计策。晋鄙的兵符平时收在魏王卧室内；如姬最得魏王宠爱，出入卧内，有能力偷出来。侯嬴说，如姬的父亲被人所杀，她为此出资三年，从魏王以下都想替她报父仇而未能；如姬向无忌哭诉，无忌派门客斩了仇人的头献给她。侯嬴的判断是：如姬愿为公子死，只是没有机会；公子一开口，她必答应。得虎符，夺晋鄙军，北救赵而西却秦，「此五霸之伐也」。

Back at the Yimen, Hou Ying laid out a plan. Jin Pi's command tally was normally kept in the king of Wei's bedchamber. Lady Ru, the king's favorite, came and went in the bedchamber freely and could steal it out. Hou Ying spelled out why she would. Her father had been murdered; for three years she had put up money to see her father's death avenged, and no one, the king included, had been able to bring it off. She had wept to Wuji, who sent a retainer to cut off her enemy's head and present it to her. Hou Ying's judgment was that Lady Ru would gladly die for Wuji and had simply never had the chance to serve him; one word from the prince and she would agree. Get the tally, take over Jin Pi's army, go north to rescue Zhao and push Qin back from the west — "an achievement worthy of the Five Hegemons."
这次朱亥答得干脆：我是市井里操刀的屠户，公子几次来问候我，我不回谢，是以为小礼无用；如今公子有急，正是我效命的时候。侯嬴则请求算着无忌的行程，在无忌抵达晋鄙军中的那天，北向自刭相送。《史记》记，后来侯嬴果然「北鄉自剄」。

This time Zhu Hai answered without hesitation: "I am a knife-wielding butcher in the market. You have come to see me in person again and again, and I never answered in kind because small courtesies are of no use. Now that you are in a fix, this is the moment for me to give my life." Hou Ying, for his part, asked to reckon the days of Wuji's journey: on the day Wuji reached Jin Pi's army he would cut his own throat facing north, to see him off. The Records later confirms that Hou Ying did cut his throat facing north.

赵孝成王感激他矫令夺兵而存赵，与平原君商量，要拿五座城封给他。无忌听说，「意驕矜而有自功之色」。一位门客劝他：别人对你有德，不可忘；你对别人有德，最好忘掉。矫魏王令、夺晋鄙兵，「於趙則有功矣，於魏則未為忠臣也」，还自骄自功，我私下以为不可取。无忌「立自責，似若無所容者」。后来赵王以主人之礼相迎，无忌侧身辞让，自言有罪过，「以負於魏，無功於趙」。赵王因他退让，口不忍献五城，最后把鄗给他作汤沐邑，魏国也把信陵还给他。

King Xiaocheng of Zhao, grateful that Wuji had seized the army on a forged order and saved Zhao, took counsel with Lord Pingyuan and proposed to enfeoff him with five cities. When Wuji heard, he "showed a self-satisfied look, as if the credit were his own." A retainer came to him: kindness done to you must never be forgotten, he said; kindness you do to another is best forgotten. Forging the king of Wei's order and seizing Jin Pi's army — "toward Zhao you have done a service; toward Wei you cannot be called a loyal minister." To go on preening yourself over it is something I cannot approve. Wuji "at once blamed himself, as if there were nowhere he could hide." Later, when the king of Zhao received him with the rites of a host, Wuji stood to the side, declined the honor, and pronounced himself at fault: "I have failed Wei and done nothing for Zhao." Because Wuji held back, the king of Zhao could not bring himself to hand over the five cities. In the end the king gave him the town of Hao to support his household, and Wei restored to him the city of Xinling.
魏王对他盗兵符、矫杀晋鄙，是发怒的，无忌自己也清楚。秦军退去之后，他让将领把魏军带回魏国，自己与门客留在赵国。后来平原君讥笑他与赌徒、卖浆的人交游，他辞别姐姐要离开时说「始吾聞平原君賢，故負魏王而救趙，以稱平原君」——当初听说平原君贤明，才辜负魏王去救赵，好配得上平原君。

The king of Wei was angry over the stolen tally and the killing of Jin Pi, and Wuji knew it. Once Qin had been driven off and Zhao saved, he sent the Wei generals home with their troops and stayed on in Zhao with his own retainers. Later, when Lord Pingyuan sneered at him for keeping company with gamblers and ale-sellers, Wuji took leave of his sister to depart and said that he had first heard Lord Pingyuan was worthy, and so had failed the king of Wei to save Zhao, to live up to Lord Pingyuan.
作者推断：把这件事读成“为朋友两肋插刀”，会错过它真正的难处。无忌折回夷门，本是问侯嬴自己有何过失；侯嬴却借这次折返点破赴死无益。侯嬴那句「譬若以肉投餒虎，何功之有哉？尚安事客？」把勇气换成了计算：百余乘车骑投进秦军能换来什么？连门客都用不上，还要门客做什么。

The author's inference: treat this as a friend staking everything for a friend and you miss where the real difficulty lay. Wuji turned back at the Yimen to ask Hou Ying what fault he had committed; Hou Ying used that return to show him that riding to his death would accomplish nothing. His rebuke — it would be like throwing meat at a starving tiger; what would it accomplish, and what use would retainers be then? — traded courage for arithmetic: what would a hundred-odd chariots buy against the Qin army? If even his retainers could not be put to use, what were retainers for?
第二步是给坏情况留人手。侯嬴提醒无忌，兵符合上，晋鄙也可能不交兵权，并让他带上朱亥；无忌听后预见到这一步要杀本国的老将，所以先流泪说破。作者推断：把代价先讲明，事到临头就不是意外，而是执行——这并不等于代价变小了。

Second, the bad case was staffed before anyone acted. Hou Ying warned Wuji that even with the tally matched, Jin Pi might refuse to hand over the army, and told him to bring Zhu Hai; hearing this, Wuji foresaw that the step would mean killing an old general of his own state, and wept and said so out loud first. The author's inference: naming the cost in advance does not make it smaller. It turns a shock into an execution of a decision already made.
第三步是事成之后怎么记账。赵要封五城，门客提醒他对魏算不得忠臣，他立刻自责；在赵王面前自言负魏、无功于赵；留赵期间还说自己负魏王而救赵。作者推断：从这些言行看，这笔债他没有抹掉，军队送回魏国，自己留在赵国。不过原文也写，他留赵十年不归；魏王遣使来请，他怕魏王发怒，还禁止门下为魏使通报，留赵未必就是认下这笔债。

Third, he kept the books honestly after it worked. Zhao was about to grant five cities; a retainer reminded him that he could not count as a loyal minister to Wei, and he blamed himself on the spot. Before the king of Zhao he declared he had failed Wei and done nothing for Zhao. While he was staying in Zhao he still said he had failed his king to save Zhao. On this reading he did not write the debt off: the army went home to Wei, and he stayed in Zhao. But the record also says he stayed in Zhao ten years without returning; when the king of Wei sent men to fetch him, he feared the king's anger and even barred his household from admitting the king's envoys, so staying there need not count as settling the debt.
另一种做法是继续等魏王回心转意。但平原君已经说邯郸旦暮降秦，拖下去的代价由城里的人承担。作者推断：他选的不是一个干净的选项，而是当时能改变局面的一种做法，代价是杀本国将军、失信于魏王。

The other course was to keep waiting for the king of Wei to change his mind. But Lord Pingyuan had already said that Handan might surrender to Qin any day, and the price of holding back would be paid by the people inside the walls. On this reading, what Wuji chose was not a clean option; it was one that could change the situation, at the price of killing his own general and losing the trust of his king.

司马迁怎么看待此事？太史公说自己过大梁，特意去寻夷门；他称无忌为信陵君，说无忌结交岩穴隐者、不耻下交，「名冠諸侯，不虛耳」。作者认为，这份褒扬落在无忌敬重侯嬴这类隐士的一端，而不在矫令杀将上。代价也没有就此结束：无忌留赵十年，后来秦攻魏，他在赵国结交的隐士毛公、薛公劝他：公子在赵国受重视、名闻诸侯，「徒以有魏也」——只因背后有魏国。他立刻归国为将，率五国之兵破秦；秦用重金收买晋鄙的门客毁谤他，魏王果然派人代将，他谢病饮酒，四年后病酒而死。他死后秦攻魏，拔二十城，此后十八年，秦国俘虏了魏王。一种解释是，这段收尾把无忌的存亡与魏国的存亡写在了一起。

What did Sima Qian make of it? The Grand Historian writes that he passed through Daliang and made a point of finding the Yimen. Calling Wuji by his title, Lord Xinling, he says Wuji's readiness to seek out recluses in mountain caves and to befriend men beneath him had good cause, and that his name stood first among the lords — no empty fame. One reading is that this praise lands on the end where Wuji honored recluses like Hou Ying, not on the forged order and the slain general. And the costs did not stop there. Wuji stayed in Zhao ten years. When Qin attacked Wei, Master Mao and Master Xue, two recluses he had befriended in Zhao, told him that he was valued in Zhao and known among the lords only because he had Wei behind him. He went home at once to command Wei's army and led the forces of five states to defeat Qin. Qin then spent heavy sums of gold buying off Jin Pi's former retainers to slander him; the king of Wei did send a replacement to take over the army, and Wuji excused himself on illness and took to drink, dying of it four years later. After his death Qin attacked Wei and took twenty cities, and eighteen years later captured the king of Wei. On one interpretation, this closing episode writes Wuji's survival and Wei's survival on the same line.
本文只依据《史记·魏公子列传》。侯嬴献计、朱亥的答话、门客的劝谏，都是史家记述的对话，未必是逐字实录。

This piece draws only on the "Biography of the Prince of Wei" in the Records of the Grand Historian. Hou Ying's plan, Zhu Hai's reply, and the retainer's remonstrance are all speeches recorded by the historian, not necessarily verbatim transcripts.
原文里的「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」是叙述用语，不是实录的心理；本文凡涉情绪处都只是转述史家的叙述。

Phrases in the original such as "troubled in his heart," "showed a self-satisfied look," and "at once blamed himself" are narrative wording, not recorded states of mind; wherever emotion enters this piece, it is only the historian's narration being relayed.
本文所用「得選兵八萬人」之数出自本传。纪年只用原文的魏安釐王二十年，不作换算。
The figure of "eighty thousand selected men" used here comes from this biography. Dates follow the original reckoning — the twentieth year of King Anxi of Wei — with no conversion.
本文只依据《史记·魏公子列传》；对话出自史家记述，未必逐字；「心不快」「意驕矜」「立自責」是叙述用语，而非实录心理；纪年只用原文，不换算公元。

This piece draws only on the "Biography of the Prince of Wei" in the Records of the Grand Historian; the speeches come from the historian's account and need not be verbatim. "Troubled in his heart," "showed a self-satisfied look," and "at once blamed himself" are narrative wording, not recorded states of mind. Dates follow the original and are not converted to the common era.

evidence.quote: 晉鄙合符，疑之
勒兵下令軍中曰

dispositions.rationale: 压缩为：只依据本传，对话未必逐字，情绪词是叙述用语，纪年不换算。删去各项“无更多记载”的说法，引语改为证据中的繁体逐字形式。

evidence.quote: 北鄉自剄，以送公子

dispositions.rationale: 驳回需要逐字证据，但这是标签问题，证据无法证明；按“拿不准就修改”处理。英文改为 The author's inference:，与中文“作者推断”一致，也不再让人误读为“这种读法本身是错的”。
